audit_findings.title: Debt may be double-counted against an after-interest earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: $455.0 million debt deduction; $14.1 million FY2025 net interest expense, or $10.7 million after tax at 24.0%; removing the debt deduction would add $7.31 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If owner earnings retains after-tax interest expense, it is an equity cash-flow numerator and deducting debt again in the bridge double-counts financing
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense, net for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $1.6 million, or 13%, compared to the prior year, largely due to higher average debt levels associated with the funding of acquisitions in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that net income is after interest and that the bridge deducts $455.0 million of debt, but the supplied record does not show whether the owner-earnings build added back after-tax interest. The error is therefore unresolved rather than demonstrated. Its maximum direct bridge effect is about 9.8% of the $74.93 base value per share, large enough to require resolution even though it would not by itself lift the bull value above the $115.12 market price.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 owner-earnings worksheet, identify the treatment of the $14.1 million interest expense, and rerun consistently as either unlevered OE plus net debt or levered OE without a debt deduction.

audit_findings.title: The June-2026 bridge may not match the FY2025 earnings perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 included only $21.2 million of New Way sales and $1.4 million of operating income, while Mega contributed $23.9 million of sales and $5.3 million of operating income from January 16 through June 30, 2026; a $13.0 million New Way closing-adjustment liability was also recorded
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor excludes full-period earnings from recently acquired businesses while the June 2026 bridge reflects their ownership, acquisition financing and liabilities
audit_findings.evidence: As the acquisition closed on November 25, 2025, the assets and liabilities of New Way have been consolidated into the Company’s Consolidated Balance Sheet as of December 31, 2025, while the post-acquisition results of operations have been included in the Consolidated Statement of Operations, within the Environmental Solutions Group.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter inconsistency, not merely a hypothetical one: New Way and Kinloch entered FY2025 results only after their late-2025 closing dates, Mega entered after year-end, and the June 2026 balance sheet includes all three. The omitted full-period earnings are not disclosed sufficiently to compute a valuation adjustment, but the size of New Way and the acquisition financing makes the mismatch reasonably capable of materially understating value. The separate $13.0 million payable partly offsets that direction but does not resolve the larger missing-earnings issue.
audit_findings.action: Construct same-perimeter OE using pro-forma or trailing-twelve-month results for New Way, Kinloch and Mega, reconcile all acquisition debt and the $13.0 million payable, and rerun every scenario on that synchronized perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Rental-fleet investment may be mistaken for working capital rather than recurring capital expenditure
audit_findings.magnitude: $55.9 million FY2025 rental-equipment cash outflow, equal to 20.4% of the $273.5 million OE anchor; maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Rental-fleet purchases are recurring investment needed to sustain rental income but appear within operating cash flow rather than conventional property capital expenditures
audit_findings.evidence: The related cash flow activity associated with these transactions is reflected within operating activities on the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate recurring rental-equipment outflows of $55.9 million in 2025, $60.3 million in 2024 and $44.8 million in 2023. They do not demonstrate whether the OE calculation retained those outflows or normalized them away. Because the 2025 amount is one-fifth of the anchor, omission of even a substantial maintenance portion could materially overstate OE and all scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Trace the rental-equipment line through the OE worksheet, separate growth additions, transfers, disposals and maintenance replacement spending, then rerun using a filed-history-supported maintenance amount.

audit_findings.title: Earn-out obligations ahead of common equity are absent from the stated bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.0 million June 2026 fair-value liability, equal to $0.24 per share and 0.32% of the $4,667 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid contingent consideration is a debt-like claim that should reduce the equity bridge unless already captured elsewhere
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had contingent obligations to transfer up to $ 3.9 million, $ 4.8 million, $ 15.0 million, and $ 54.0 million to the former owners of Blasters, Standard, Hog, and New Way, respectively, if specified financial results are met over future reporting periods (i.e., an earn-out).
audit_findings.explanation: The June filing reports $15.0 million of contingent consideration, while the stated bridge contains no earn-out deduction. Even deducting the entire filed fair-value liability would reduce base value only from $74.93 to approximately $74.69 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $115.12 price. The $58.8 million maximum contractual payouts are not an appropriate quantified liability because achievement probabilities are not established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $4.3 million current and $10.7 million long-term components to the bridge and document whether the $15.0 million fair-value liability is deducted elsewhere.

audit_findings.title: Serial-acquisition costs may have been stripped despite being part of the growth model
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.0 million FY2025 acquisition and integration expense, including $6.8 million of contingent-consideration remeasurement; recurring normalized portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding acquisition costs back to OE while relying on acquisition-driven growth preserves the acquired earnings but removes the recurring costs required to obtain and integrate them
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we have completed 15 acquisitions since 2016.
audit_findings.explanation: The company completed 15 acquisitions since 2016 and reported $16.0 million of acquisition and integration expense in 2025, so recurring deal execution is plausible. The record does not show whether the valuation added this expense back, whether scenario growth requires further acquisitions, or what portion represents recurring cash costs rather than noncash earn-out remeasurement. Accordingly, an overstatement is possible, but materiality cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every FY2025 OE adjustment to the $16.0 million line, isolate the $6.8 million remeasurement and other noncash items, map scenario growth between organic and acquired sources, and rerun with recurring cash deal costs matched to acquisition-dependent growth.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded employee-benefit claims may be missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $44.4 million gross June 2026 long-term pension and other post-retirement liability, equal to $0.71 per share and 0.95% of the $4,667 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Net unfunded pension, deferred-compensation and similar employee claims reduce value reaching common equity unless offset by specifically attributable assets or captured elsewhere
audit_findings.evidence: Deferred compensation liabilities were $ 26.9 million as of December 31, 2025 and $ 23.6 million as of December 31, 2024, and were included on the Consolidated Balance Sheets, primarily within Long-term pension and other post-retirement benefit liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The stated bridge omits the filed $44.4 million aggregate liability. Even deducting that entire gross line without credit for any offsetting plan assets would reduce base value only from $74.93 to approximately $74.22 per share and would not alter the conclusion relative to the $115.12 price. The proper net claim is smaller or equal because the December filing separately reported a $10.8 million overfunded foreign-plan asset.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 deferred-compensation balance and pension funded-status schedules, match specifically restricted plan assets against the liabilities, and document the resulting net debt-like amount in the bridge.
